query: What happens to precision laboratory instruments when they are moved routinely rather than left in place: analytical and micro balances, optical microscopes and profilometers, tabletop SEMs, X-ray diffractometers and XRF, nanoindenters and hardness testers, laser-diffraction particle sizers, potentiostats. Shock and vibration limits in transport versus in operation, loss of levelling or calibration after a move and the requalification or settling and warm-up time needed (for example balance guidance in USP <41> and <1251>, OIML R 76, manufacturers' relocation guidance), and evidence from instruments mounted on moving platforms such as mobile laboratories, ships, vehicles, AGVs or automated storage systems.
